content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed its first set of guidelines aimed at transforming and scaling up the education and training of health professionals. These guidelines are intended to stimulate regional and national policy discussions among key stakeholders in education, health, finance, and labor sectors. The goal is to identify effective strategies for financing health professionals' training and preparing them to meet the demands of 21st-century healthcare. The guidelines are based on the latest evidence and emphasize the need to address the global health workforce crisis, which affects 57 countries severely, as highlighted in the 2006 World Health Report. However, workforce shortages, skill imbalances, and uneven geographic distribution of health professionals are challenges faced by nearly every country. These issues leave millions without access to essential health services. Addressing these challenges requires not only increasing the number of health workers but also improving the quality and relevance of their training to meet population health needs. Educational institutions must expand their capacity, improve faculty competencies, reform admissions criteria, and regularly update curricula to align with the burden of disease and training needs. Pathways should also be created for mid-career professionals or students from other disciplines to transition into health professions. The international community is encouraged to support country-led efforts to implement these reforms. The guidelines advocate for strong political commitment and collaboration between education and health sectors, as well as other national authorities and the private sector. This collaboration aims to align health professionals' education with the realities of healthcare delivery. Recommendations include fostering community engagement, developing relevant curricula, and equipping health professionals with the skills to work in underserved areas. Transformative scaling up of health professionals' education is defined as the sustainable expansion and reform of education and training to increase the quantity, quality, and relevance of health professionals. This process strengthens national health systems and improves population health outcomes. The guidelines provide evidence-informed recommendations to guide this transformation globally. Key recommendations include: 1. Continuous faculty development programs to address evolving healthcare needs. 2. Mandatory faculty development policies supported by governments and accrediting bodies. 3. Innovative faculty expansion through the recruitment of community-based clinicians and health workers as educators. 4. Adapting curricula to meet the changing healthcare needs of communities. 5. Utilizing simulation methods in education, tailored to resource availability. 6. Direct entry pathways for graduates from relevant educational programs into professional studies. 7. Targeted admissions policies to increase diversity among students. 8. Streamlined educational pathways and ladder programs for advancing practicing health professionals. 9. Implementation of inter-professional education in undergraduate and postgraduate programs. 10. Establishing or strengthening accreditation systems for health professionals' education. 11. Continuous professional development and in-service training for health professionals. The guidelines emphasize the importance of aligning educational institutions with healthcare systems to prepare graduates who are motivated to work in rural and underserved areas. This alignment is critical for addressing health equity and ensuring that health professionals are equipped to meet the needs of diverse populations. The WHO initiative on transforming and scaling up health professionals' education represents a significant contribution to reshaping the global health workforce. It aims to produce graduates who are responsive to the health needs of the populations they serve, thereby contributing to sustainable health systems and improved health outcomes worldwide.
